call_points.text: FY27 guidance maintained: ₹6,000 Cr presales from owned projects, ₹2,000 Cr from development management and ₹3,000 Cr collections.
Q1 presales ₹868 Cr, up 338% YoY; collections ₹496 Cr, up 54% YoY.
Construction spend in Q1 was ₹276 Cr, about 56% of collections.
Gross institutional debt about ₹4,500 Cr, cash about ₹1,200 Cr, net debt about ₹3,300 Cr at 0.35x net debt to equity.
Net loss widened to ₹234 Cr from ₹166 Cr a year ago on completion-based revenue recognition.
Q1 operating cash flow was negative ₹285 Cr as no projects were launched; collections expected to turn positive from Q2.
Bangalore building plan approvals delayed by GBA not meeting; launches may slip a quarter.
Nashik land debonding to take another 6 to 9 months; company seeking amicable solution with MIDC.
Company exploring percentage completion method of accounting, to review over next couple of quarters.
Gross institutional debt stands at approximately ₹4,100 crores with cash of ₹1,100 crores, yielding net institutional debt of ₹3,000 crores.

operating_notes.text: Subsidiary EEBPL retains possession of 78 acres of land at Kadugodi Industrial Area, Bengaluru after High Court sets aside KIADB resumption order.
Preferential issue proceeds fully utilized at ₹3,510.66 Cr following lapse of unexercised warrants worth ₹397.48 Cr.
Appointed Chirag Boonlia as Chief Technology Officer.
FY26 construction spend stood at ₹1,182 crores, representing about 71% of collections.
Q1FY27 presales ₹868 Cr and collections ₹496 Cr; construction spend ₹276 Cr, about 56% of collections.
FY27 launch pipeline: 11 projects with GDV ₹19,400 Cr (9 owned at ₹13,300 Cr, 2 development management at ₹6,000-plus Cr); four launches planned in Q2FY27.
Cumulative unsold inventory across launched and under-construction portfolio is ₹13,630 Cr; ongoing development portfolio of 11 assets is about 70% sold by saleable area.

timeline.summary: Embassy Developments announced that NCLAT reserved its order on the CIRP admission appeal, with the stay on insolvency proceedings continuing.
Embassy Developments announced that NCLAT allowed its appeal, setting aside the NCLT order and quashing the CIRP proceedings against the company.
Embassy Developments announced that the Karnataka High Court set aside the KIADB order, allowing EEBPL's writ petition and protecting its 78-acre land holding in Bengaluru.
Embassy Developments filed its Q4FY26 monitoring agency report showing full utilization of ₹3,510.66 Cr preferential issue proceeds.

Embassy Developments Limited’s **Aditya Virwani (Promoter, MD), Sachin Shah (CEO & ED), and Rajesh Kaimal (CFO & ED)** will host an earnings conference call on **May 21, 2026, at 11:00 AM (IST)** to discuss Q4 & FY2026 performance.
On May 21, 2026, Embassy Developments hosted its Q4 and FY26 earnings conference call, guiding for ₹6,000 Cr in FY27 presales.

Embassy Developments reported Q1FY27 presales of ₹868 Cr (up 338% YoY) and collections of ₹496 Cr (up 54% YoY), with a net loss of ₹234 Cr, and its board approved preferential warrants to Embassy Group at ₹111.51 per share to repay ₹363 Cr of shareholder debt.
Embassy Developments allotted 1.10 crore equity shares upon warrant conversion, raising ₹92 Cr and increasing promoter holding to 43.13%.
On October 27, 2026, Embassy Developments allotted 1,22,00,000 equity shares upon warrant conversion, raising ₹102 Cr.
